_1password.steps: 1Password connects through a Connect server that your 1Password admin runs. They create it in 1Password.com under Developer, along with an access token for it.

full.label: Connect server address
full.help: The web address of your Connect server, for example https://connect.example.com. Your 1Password admin can tell you what it is.

generic_api_key.label: Access token
generic_api_key.help: The access token made for that Connect server. Your 1Password admin can find it in 1Password.com under Developer, then Connect servers.

openai.steps: Create a secret key on the API keys page of your OpenAI account.

posthog.steps: In PostHog, open Settings, then Personal API keys, and create a key. Copy it straight away, because PostHog shows it only once.

sendgrid.steps: In SendGrid, open Settings, then API Keys, and create a key with full access. Copy it straight away, because SendGrid shows it only once.

elevenlabs.steps: Create an API key in your ElevenLabs account and copy it straight away, because it's shown only once.

firecrawl.steps: Sign in to Firecrawl and copy your key from the API Keys page.

tavily.steps: Sign in to Tavily and copy a key from the API Keys section.

serpapi.steps: Sign in to SerpApi and copy your private API key.

perplexityai.steps: Create an API key in your Perplexity account and copy it straight away, because it's shown only once.

exa.steps: Sign in to Exa and create or copy a key on the API keys page.

cloudflare.steps: Copy the Global API Key from your Cloudflare profile, and enter the email address you sign in to Cloudflare with.

pandadoc.steps: Create an API key in your PandaDoc account. The link shows how.

mixpanel.steps: In Mixpanel, open Organization Settings, then Service Accounts, and create one. Copy its secret straight away, because it's shown only once.

algolia.steps: Copy your Application ID and an API key from the Algolia dashboard. A search-only key is enough for reading.

apify.steps: In Apify Console, open Settings, then API & Integrations, and copy your API token.

apollo.steps: In Apollo, open Settings, then Integrations, then API Keys, and create a key. Turn on Set as master key so every action works.

replicate.steps: Sign in to Replicate and copy a token from the API tokens page.

deepgram.steps: Create an API key in the Deepgram console.

datadog.steps: In Datadog, open Organization Settings. Copy an API key from API Keys and an application key from Application Keys.

telegram.steps: In Telegram, message @BotFather and send /newbot to make a bot and get its token. This connects a bot, not your own Telegram account.

shortcut.steps: Create an API token in your Shortcut settings.

toggl.steps: Copy the API token from your Toggl Track profile settings.

cloudinary.steps: Copy your cloud name, API key and API secret from the Cloudinary console.

postmark.steps: In Postmark, open your server, then the API Tokens tab, and copy the Server API token.

amplitude.steps: Copy your project's API key and secret key from Amplitude.

segment.steps: Create a Public API token in your Segment workspace.

close.steps: In Close, open Settings, then Developer, then API Keys, and create a key. Copy it straight away, because it's shown in full only once.

ashby.steps: An Ashby admin creates the key under Admin, then Integrations, then API Keys. Copy it straight away, because it's shown only once.

assemblyai.steps: In the AssemblyAI dashboard, open Workspace, then Manage, then API Keys, and copy a key for the project you want to use.

freshdesk.steps: In Freshdesk, open your profile picture, then Profile Settings, and select View API key.

heygen.steps: In HeyGen, open Settings, then API, and copy your key.

mem0.steps: Copy an API key from your Mem0 settings.

browserbase_tool.steps: Sign in to Browserbase and copy your API key from Settings.
